prompts:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: standalone cinematic background artwork for a software engineer portfolio.
Primary request: a beautiful realistic developer workstation at dusk, photographed with refined restrained luxury and rich spatial depth.
Scene/backdrop: modern charcoal interior, glass windows overlooking softly blurred dusk city lights on the right.
Subject: on the right side, a warm walnut desk with ultrawide monitors showing abstract unreadable code shapes and a mountain wallpaper, a warm sculptural desk lamp, restrained green plants and tactile desk objects.
Style/medium: high-end architectural interior photography, cinematic realism, physically plausible materials, subtle film grain, meticulous detail.
Composition/framing: widescreen 16:9 landscape. Right-heavy workstation composition. Keep the left 45 percent as quiet, almost-black empty charcoal wall with no objects, reserved for HTML headline overlay. Desk and windows occupy the right 55 percent, with elegant depth and soft perspective. All four corners fade gently into black.
Lighting/mood: warm amber practical lighting, soft dusk illumination, deep rich shadows, sophisticated quiet atmosphere.
Color palette: near-black charcoal, warm amber, muted walnut, very subtle steel blue dusk.
Constraints: no people, no readable text, no logos, no watermark, no typography, no website UI, no borders. Generate only the standalone artwork.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: standalone wide cinematic architectural background artwork for a software engineer portfolio.
Primary request: a compelling physically rendered architectural installation of large translucent smoked-glass panels aligned in depth.
Scene/backdrop: a dark monumental charcoal interior, subtle charcoal stone floor and wall.
Subject: tall smoked-glass slabs in a precise architectural sequence, layered perspective and elegant negative space; fine warm amber glowing edges create quiet luminous lines through the dark glass.
Style/medium: photorealistic premium architectural photograph and physically plausible rendering, refined restrained luxury, realistic spatial depth, subtle textures and reflections.
Composition/framing: widescreen landscape approximately 16:9. Installation concentrated in the right 55 percent, with overlapping panels receding in depth. Left 45 percent is quiet almost-black negative space, reserved for HTML text. Fade peripheral edges gently to black.
Lighting/mood: dramatic shadow, restrained warm amber volumetric light, dark calm atmosphere, natural reflections on translucent glass.
Color palette: near-black charcoal, smoked black glass, subtle stone gray, warm amber highlights.
Constraints: no people, no diagrams, no text, no labels, no interface, no website UI, no logos, no watermark, no typography. Generate only the standalone artwork.

Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: standalone wide cinematic Earth-at-night background artwork for a software engineer portfolio.
Primary request: photorealistic Earth limb at night rising diagonally from the lower right across a deep black field.
Subject: the curving nighttime surface of Earth with realistic warm gold urban lights and a very fine atmospheric rim, subtle cloud texture over a dark ocean and land mass.
Style/medium: cinematic space photography, physically realistic globe curvature, refined restrained luxury, exquisite subtle detail.
Composition/framing: widescreen landscape approximately 16:9. Earth occupies the lower right and right edge with a diagonal rising curved limb. Keep most of the left half completely black and calm, reserved for HTML contact copy. Globe edges naturally dissolve into darkness.
Lighting/mood: deep near-black space with soft warm golden city illumination and a fine subdued pale atmospheric rim, no bright sun.
Color palette: deep black, near-black charcoal planet, warm gold urban lights, very subtle muted atmospheric blue.
Constraints: no labels, no connecting lines, no constellation lines, no HUD, no text, no interface, no typography, no logos, no watermark, no people. Generate only the standalone artwork.
